hero.title: Biotechnology
hero.subtitle: Earn a prestigious Biotechnology qualification in France, combining rigorous biochemical sciences, bio-industrial internships, and advanced pharmaceutical technology. Explore vibrant research opportunities across Europe's prominent biotechnology networks and healthcare innovation institutes.

overview: Students interested in studying biotechnology, life sciences, genetic engineering, pharmaceutical research, and industrial innovation will find France a most attractive destination.
Biotechnology is the collective use of biology, chemistry, genetics and technology to create products and processes for use in healthcare, agriculture, food production and environmental protection.

Studying Biotechnology in France can assist students in acquiring scientific knowledge and practical skills for careers in research, biopharmaceutical manufacturing, diagnostics and product development.

sections.title: Biotechnology Courses in France
sections.lead: \\Biotechnology courses in France\\ are available at undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral level. The right programme depends on your previous education and career goals.

items: Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology

A bachelor's degree in biotechnology or a licence level programme usually takes three years. Students can major in biotechnology at some universities, or they can start with a related degree in \\biology\\, \\life sciences\\, \\biochemistry\\ or \\molecular and cellular biology\.
Typical topics include:
\\Molecular and cellular biology.
\\Genetics and genomics.\\
Microbial.
\\Biochemistry\\
Biological sciences and chemistry.
Experimental techniques and laboratory methods.
An introduction to bioinformatics and biotechnology.
Depending on the employer's requirements, a bachelor's degree can qualify students for entry-level laboratory positions, or for higher education at the master's level.
Master's in Biotechnology

A \\master's in biotechnology\\ is a popular choice for international students if you have a relevant bachelor's degree. The standard French national master's degree is \\2 years\\ and gives \\120 ECTS credits\.
Common specialisations are:
\\Medical Biotechnology:\\ Biomedical research, diagnostics and therapeutic technologies.
\\Pharmaceutical Biotechnology:\\ Biologic drugs, Biopharmaceutical development and production.
\\Industrial Biotechnology:\\ Bioprocesses, fermentation, industrial enzymes and production technology.
\\Molecular Biotechnology:\\ Genetic engineering, cell biology, molecular biology & lab research.
\\Agricultural Biotechnology:\\ plant genetics, crop breeding and agricultural innovation
\\Environmental Biotechnology:\\ Application of biological techniques to environmental monitoring, waste treatment and sustainability.
\\Bioprocess Engineering:\\ Bioreactors, production processes, process optimization and quality assurance.
PhD Biotechnology

Students interested in research may be encouraged to pursue a \\PhD in Biotechnology\\ if they meet the academic and research requirements. Research topics can include gene therapy, synthetic biology, drug discovery, immunology, bioinformatics and industrial bioprocessing.
Course Duration Brief:
\\Bachelor's degree:\\ typically 3 years.
\\Master's degree:\\ Usually 2 years of study after a bachelor degree.
\\PhD:\\ generally 3 additional years in France depending on the project and the doctoral school.

sections.title: Eligibility to Study Biotechnology in France
sections.lead: \\Eligibility to study biotechnology in France\\ depends on the course level, academic background, language of instruction, and specific university requirements.

items: Generally applicants require:
A \\second-level school qualification\\ comparable to a French baccalauréat.
Relevant academic background in \\biology\\, \\chemistry\\, \\mathematics\\ or other related sciences.
The required \\ language skills.
Evidence of studies that meet the university's admission requirements.
Students who don't find a direct-entry biotechnology degree may consider a related \\life-sciences or biology programme\\ and specialise later.
Applicants typically will need:
An accredited \\bachelor's degree\\ in biotechnology, biotechnology engineering, biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, microbiology, pharmaceutical sciences or related discipline.
\\Academic transcripts\\ demonstrating appropriate scientific preparation.
\\Fluency in French or English\\ as appropriate for the programme.
Laboratory, research or quantitative background as needed.
Other supporting documents as required by the university.
Some programs will accept applicants with related engineering or health-science backgrounds; others require specific subject areas or prior laboratory experience.
PhD degree

Applicants usually need to have a relevant \\master's degree\\ or equivalent, an appropriate research background and a suitable \\research project or supervisor arrangement\\, depending on the doctoral school.

sections.title: Admission Requirements – Biotechnology in France
sections.lead: \\Admission requirements for biotechnology in France\\ are different for each university and programme. Applicants may be requested to provide:

items: \\Certificates and Transcripts of Study.
\\Bachelor's degree certificate\\ for masters applications.
\\CV or résumé.
A \\letter of motivation or personal statement.
\\French or English language test results\\, when required.
Academic or professional references if asked.
Documentation of relevant \\lab or research experience\\, if applicable.
\\Research proposal or supervisor agreement\\ for selected PhD programmes.
Certified translation of documents, if necessary.
\\Biotechnology programmes in France\\ can be delivered in French, English or a mix of the two. Applicants should verify the language of instruction for the course they are applying for.

For \\programmes taught in French\\, the university may ask for proof of proficiency in the French language. \\English-taught programmes\\ may require proof of proficiency via IELTS, TOEFL, or an alternative accepted test.

sections.title: Admission Process for Biotechnology in France
sections.lead: The \\application process for biotechnology in France\\ depends on the programme level, the university and the country of residence of the applicant.

items: 1. \\Specialisation:\\ Choose whether you want to specialise in \\pharmaceutical\\, \\medical\\, \\industrial\\, \\agricultural\\ or \\environmental biotechnology\.
2. \\Shortlist universities:\\ Compare course content, language requirements, tuition fees, research facilities and internship options.
3. \\Check eligibility:\\ Confirm your previous degree and academic subjects meet the entry requirements.
4. \\Define the application path:\\ Depending on the program and the applicant profile, you may have to use \\Études en France\\, \\Mon Master\\ or a specific application portal of the university.
5. \\Prepare documents:\\ Gather transcripts, degree certificates, language proof, CV and letter of motivation.
6. \\Apply:\\ follow the current deadlines and documentation instructions of the university.
7. \\Full application process:\\ Certain programmes may involve an interview, further assessment or evidence of suitable experience.
8. \ACCEPT YOUR OFFER\ Administrative registration and accommodation planning.
9. \\Arrange your student visa if needed:\\ Follow the official \\French student visa process\\ applicable to your situation.
Application Process for Indian Students

sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation of Biotechnology Degrees in France
sections.lead: Before registering, check the \\status of the qualification\\ and the institution awarding it.

items: A \\French master's degree\\ generally consists of two years of study after a bachelor's degree and \\120 ECTS credits\. Not all courses labelled as a biotechnology programme are national master's degrees, however. University diplomas, certificates in continuing education and other specialist qualifications may have a different status.
Applicants should verify:
The exact name of the qualification.
If it is a \\state degree\\ or a university diploma.
The number of \\credits\\ (ECTS) obtained.
Whether it is laboratory training, a research project or an internship.
If the qualification corresponds to their career or further study intentions.

\\Biotechnology\\ is a broad scientific discipline and many laboratory or industrial jobs are not regulated in the same way as other professions such as medicine or pharmacy. But, an employer may want specific technical skills, experience or additional qualifications.

\\For students from India:\\ If you plan to return to India, please check with the prospective employer and any relevant institution or authority in India regarding the acceptability of the degree before enrolling. Research, teaching, industry and regulated healthcare related roles may have different recognition requirements.

faqs.q: How long does it take to study Bio-technology in France?
faqs.a: A \\bachelor's degree\\ usually takes three years. A typical \\master's degree\\ takes two additional years to complete, and a \\PhD\\ normally requires three additional years, depending upon the research project.

faqs.q: Need IELTS for studying biotechnology in France?
faqs.a: Not everybody needs to sit for the IELTS. English language programmes may require IELTS, TOEFL, another accepted test or alternative evidence of proficiency in English. Instead, French-taught programmes may require proof of proficiency in French.

faqs.q: What is the cost of biotechnology in France?
faqs.a: For \\2026–2027\\ the national reference registration fee for a master's programme at a public institution is \\€255 per year\\ for eligible French/EU-category students and \\€3,950 per year\\ for applicable non-EU students. There may be exemptions. Programme-specific arrangements and living expenses are additional.

faqs.q: What jobs are there after studying biotechnology in France?
faqs.a: Graduates may work in \\biotechnology research\\, \\pharmaceutical manufacturing\\, \\bioproduction\\, quality control, diagnostics, \\clinical research\\, \\regulatory affairs\\ and \\bioinformatics. The specific requirements depend on the role and the employer.
